en.title: FX's 'Adults' Season 2 Surges 100% Internationally Amidst Critical Acclaim
en.summary: The FX sitcom 'Adults' is proving that growing up can be a ratings hit. Season two has seen a significant international viewership surge, mirroring its critical success.
en.body:
While some streaming giants grapple with second-season viewership drops for their flagship series, FX's charming sitcom **Adults** is charting a different course. The show, which follows a group of New York twentysomethings navigating the choppy waters of adulthood, has experienced a remarkable surge in its second season. According to FX, international viewership has doubled in the 12 days following its August 27, 2026 premiere, while its domestic audience on Hulu and Disney+ has grown by over 40%. This impressive uptick is particularly noteworthy when contrasted with the reported declines for shows like **Four Seasons** and **Beef** on Netflix.

This isn't just a win for **Adults**; it's a testament to its finely tuned narrative and relatable characters. The series, created by **Ben Kronengold** and **Rebecca Shaw**, premiered in May 2025 and quickly garnered critical praise. Its second season, which premiered on August 27, 2026, has achieved near-perfect scores on Rotten Tomatoes, boasting a 100% critic score and a 98% audience score. This critical adoration is well-earned, with reviewers praising its ability to balance genuine laugh-out-loud moments with surprisingly moving friendship dilemmas. The AV Club noted that the show "takes advantage of that limited time to polish its tone and hit us with amusing running gags, surprisingly moving friendship dilemmas... and, best of all, genuine laugh-out-loud moments."

## A Season of Growth and Resilience

The sophomore season of **Adults** has clearly struck a chord with viewers worldwide. The show's premise, a modern take on the classic ensemble sitcom reminiscent of **Friends**, focuses on the unwavering support system these friends provide for each other. This season, the narrative has deepened, allowing characters to explore more complex emotional arcs. For instance, the subtle realization of budding romance between best friends, as seen with Issa, adds a layer of authentic interpersonal drama that resonates deeply. The show's commitment to authentic storytelling, coupled with its sharp comedic timing, has clearly paid off, creating a loyal and expanding fanbase.

## What's Next for the **Adults** Ensemble

Despite the overwhelmingly positive reception and significant audience growth, FX has yet to officially announce a third season for **Adults**. However, given the show's critical acclaim and burgeoning global popularity, fans have reason to be optimistic. The network has previously demonstrated a willingness to invest in its acclaimed comedies, and the momentum from season two's success makes a renewal a strong possibility. Viewers can continue to stream the current season on Hulu and FX, eagerly awaiting news about the future of their favorite New York ensemble.

## Addressing Early Stumbles

It's worth noting that **Adults** has also shown a remarkable ability to adapt. Following reports that some viewers were initially put off by an over-the-top scene in the very first episode, FX took the unusual step of producing a revised version. This proactive approach to audience feedback underscores the network's belief in the show and its commitment to ensuring viewers have the best possible entry point into its world. It’s a bold move that seems to have paid off, contributing to the show's overall positive trajectory.

content_raw: The Adults are alright. In fact, they’re better than alright. The FX sitcom, which, unsurprisingly, The A.V. Club has already named one of the best and funniest shows on television , is a bona fide hit. Much like the characters who are slowly but surely learning what it takes to make it in this workaday world, the audience is growing in season two. According to FX, and taken with a grain of salt, the show’s audience has grown more than 40% on Hulu and Disney+, as international viewership grew 100% in the 12 days since its second-season premiere. It’s perhaps a reason to be optimistic, especially following reports of Netflix’s second-season crisis , which saw drops in viewership for Four Seasons , Beef , and A Man On The Inside , among others. Strangely, FX wasn’t happy enough with the audience growth to announce a third season.  Adults is a classic, Friends -style ensemble sitcom about a group of New York twentysomethings being there for each other when it hasn’t been their day, week, month, or year. We were huge fans of the show’s second season. Our TV Critic, Saloni Gajjar, wrote in her review, “It might only be eight episodes long, but Adults’ second season takes advantage of that limited time to polish its tone and hit us with amusing running gags, surprisingly moving friendship dilemmas (like Issa slowly realizing that her boyfriend and her BFF truly might be into each other!), and, best of all, genuine laugh-out-loud moments.”
